@copilot Simplify the socket-address tests in this PR directly, without changing production address support or creating another PR.

Remove the netty-transport-native-unix-common and grpc-netty-shaded testImplementation dependencies from instrumentation-api/build.gradle.kts. In instrumentation-api/src/test/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/api/semconv/network/NetworkAttributesExtractorSocketAddressTest.java, make the tests JDK-only: use JDK UnixDomainSocketAddress instances for Unix extraction, empty paths, socket-getter precedence over Inet getters, and explicit attribute overrides. Gate cases requiring that JDK type on Java 16 or newer.

Delete the Netty-specific factories, shaded/unshaded Netty cases, and optionalNettyTypesInDifferentClassLoaders test, along with unused imports and helpers. Keep Inet compatibility, unresolved-address behavior, unsupported-address behavior, and missing-runtime-capability coverage. Keep the Inet-only capability assertions runnable on older supported JDKs; gate any JDK Unix-specific assertions appropriately. Do not introduce fake Netty-named fixtures or replacement dependencies.

Do not move Netty tests into gRPC or add any gRPC dependencies. Keep the existing focused gRPC address-forwarding tests. Preserve production support for JDK, Netty, and shaded Netty addresses, the class-loader-aware cache, Android capability guards, logging, and address semantics. The user already added the Android comment in SocketAddressUtil; leave it unchanged. Dropping direct real-Netty and cross-application-class-loader test coverage is an explicitly accepted trade-off for this test-only simplification.

Apply the narrow formatting tasks and run focused instrumentation-api and gRPC tests plus the relevant Animal Sniffer compatibility checks. Keep changes limited to this simplification and preserve the PR's draft state.

replies.body: Simplified the API tests to use JDK Unix-domain addresses, removed the Netty test dependencies and fixtures, and retained gated Unix/runtime coverage plus older-JDK Inet checks. Focused API/gRPC tests, Animal Sniffer checks, Java 8 coverage, and formatting checks pass. Commit: `eacb2a5d`.

threads.body: [Testing] The new tests exercise only JDK Unix-domain addresses; neither Netty class-name branch is covered. Those tests therefore do not verify the `path(): String` lookup or the application-class-loader behavior that gRPC's Netty transports depend on. Please add extraction tests using both ordinary and grpc-netty-shaded `DomainSocketAddress` instances, including isolated application loaders, and assert the paths, `unix` transport, and absence of ports/IP versions.

replies.body: This coverage was intentionally removed in eacb2a5d to keep the shared API tests JDK-only and eliminate the two transport test dependencies. JDK tests retain Unix path/transport, empty-path, override, and runtime-guard coverage, and the production Netty lookup code is unchanged by this cleanup. Direct Netty signature and application-class-loader coverage is a known, accepted trade-off for this simplification, so we're not restoring those tests here.

@copilot Restore focused real-Netty socket-address coverage in this PR directly. The user has reconsidered the earlier JDK-only test simplification and now wants to keep both ordinary Netty and gRPC-shaded Netty support in the shared SocketAddressUtil, with tests for both.

In instrumentation-api/src/test/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/api/semconv/network/NetworkAttributesExtractorSocketAddressTest.java, restore extraction tests using actual io.netty.channel.unix.DomainSocketAddress and io.grpc.netty.shaded.io.netty.channel.unix.DomainSocketAddress instances. Assert the decoded local/peer paths, unix transport, omitted ports and IP versions, and empty-path behavior. Reuse the existing shared Unix assertions rather than duplicating the full Inet/override test matrix.

Restore the optionalNettyTypesInDifferentClassLoaders coverage removed by eacb2a5dc97d0cb0a8523434090788180175572f. Exercise both supported Netty names from isolated application class loaders against the same shared helper, including separate runtime classes with the same name, so one cached application accessor cannot accidentally serve another loader. The previous tests and dependencies can be found at bb813fc9bfe19e1acc0bd95fbd59544f283db6f1. Use real dependency classes, not fake fixtures under Netty package names.

Restore the needed test-only netty-transport-native-unix-common and grpc-netty-shaded dependencies in instrumentation-api/build.gradle.kts. Keep runtime dependencies unchanged. Retain the current JDK Unix tests, Java 16 gates, Inet compatibility, unsupported/unresolved address checks, explicit override behavior, and missing-runtime-capability coverage. Keep the tests as small as these distinct compatibility behaviors permit.

Do not change production decoding, the nullable ClassValue cache, Android capability guards or the user's Android comment. Keep both Netty class-name branches in shared code. Leave gRPC production code and its tests unchanged, do not move these tests to gRPC, and do not deprecate the old Inet getters in this PR. Apply the narrow formatting task and run the focused instrumentation-api tests and relevant Animal Sniffer checks, including the repository's existing Java 8 test execution where available. Preserve the PR's draft state.

replies.body: Restored both real Netty address variants, their Unix/empty-path extraction assertions, and isolated-loader coverage for both shaded and unshaded types. Restored test-only dependencies; no production decoding or gRPC code changed. Commit: `8f3211a1`. Focused tests, Java 8 execution, Animal Sniffer, and Spotless pass.
Removed the redundant test class in commit `05f400fb`. The gRPC 1.6 library tests pass.

Maybe we should also have a custom class to represent domain socket address. Then instrumentation could convert from whatever library uses to our representation in case we don’t handle whatever library uses.

replies.body: Updated both precedence tests to use `nettyAddress(false, ...)`, removed their JDK 16 gates and unnecessary `throws Exception` clauses, and kept the JDK Unix coverage gated. Focused tests and formatting pass. Commit: `fd5a992e`.
Updated in `2488381e`: all three tests now use try-with-resources, and the reflective `close(URLClassLoader)` helper was removed. Focused tests pass on Java 25 and Java 8.

threads.body: [General] This lookup supports only the bootstrap-loaded `java.net.UnixDomainSocketAddress`, so `ClassValue` adds per-class lookups and a runtime capability requirement without class-dependent accessor metadata. Resolve the optional JDK class once without initialization in the lazy holder, cache one nullable method handle, and check the address type before invoking it. Remove the unused `ClassValue` capability probe and its corresponding runtime-guard test cases in `NetworkAttributesExtractorSocketAddressTest`.

replies.body: Fixed in c8a3a4ed4f. The shared extractor now loads `UnixDomainSocketAddress` once without initializing it, caches one `getPath()` handle, and checks the address type before using it. I removed the shared `ClassValue` probe and its test cases. The gRPC cache is unchanged because Netty addresses can come from different class loaders.

threads.body: [General] With two named Netty Unix endpoints, network attribute extraction invokes this method handle and allocates a new wrapper eight times per span, including for type and port lookups that do not need the path. Normalize each endpoint once when it is captured in `GrpcRequest`, or cache a normalized value alongside the raw address, and have both gRPC network getters reuse it. Preserve the existing public socket-address getters' behavior and refresh any cached value when an endpoint is updated.

replies.body: Fixed in `a51ce6e8e8`. `GrpcRequest` now normalizes each Netty Unix endpoint when it captures or updates the address, and both client and server telemetry reuse that result. That cuts eight conversions to two for two named Unix endpoints. The public getters still return the original addresses.
